service.description: The buying policy of an organization in effect at a date (design-purchasing PurchasePolicy): each value, the built-in default where the row in effect sets none (traceRows has the display text and the source), the row in effect (policyFromDate, the row a document keeps; configuredPolicy and expectedFromDate for its form), the organization's rows newest first (history) and whether the user may change them. The approval gate's flag (approvalGateEnabled), self-approval, supplier approval, the unapproved supplier's Warn or Stop and the RFQ, quote-expiry and reminder days are the controls later phases read. Requires PURCHASE_POLICY_EDIT, PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT, PURCHASE_APPROVE, PURCHASE_ORDER_APPROVE or SUPPLIER_PROFILE_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE). A rule that runs as any user (a SECA) reads it through PurchasePolicy.js's effective(), which checks no permission.

parameter.name: organizationPartyId
parameter.description: The user's active or first organization when empty

parameter.name: policy
parameter.description: The value of each field in effect

service.description: A dated buying policy change for an organization: the buying defaults (currency, purchase price list, receiving facility, default buyer, payment term, Incoterm) and the purchase controls (RFQ response days, quote-expiry warning days, acknowledgement reminder days, sent orders by revision, supplier approval required, the unapproved supplier's Warn or Stop, the approval gate and self-approval). An empty value takes the built-in default. The row in effect at the start ends there; the new row holds its values with the changes, every field audit-logged with the reason, and the earlier row stays with its history. A document keeps the row it was evaluated against. Requires PURCHASE_POLICY_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), a stale expectedFromDate (POLICY_CHANGED), a start before now, a second row at the same time and an invalid value (POLICY_INVALID).

parameter.name: expectedFromDate
parameter.description: The fromDate of the row in effect when the form was read, empty when none

parameter.name: policyGroup
parameter.description: defaults or controls: only that group's fields change (one PurchasePolicy form); empty changes every field given

service.description: Whether an organization may send a supplier an RFQ or a purchase order at a date (now by default), for the order and RFQ services beside check#ProductUsable: a purchase block in effect on the organization's SupplierProfile (SUPPLIER_BLOCKED) or a Suspended profile (SUPPLIER_SUSPENDED) stops; a supplier that is not Approved (Pending, Rejected, or with no status where the policy requires approval) gets the policy's result, WARN by default or STOP (SUPPLIER_UNAPPROVED); otherwise OK. A supplier with no profile and a policy that does not require approval is OK, as before Purchasing. It refuses nothing itself: the caller stops on STOP and shows the message on WARN, and keeps policyFromDate. Requires a purchasing permission as get#PurchasePolicy does (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE) and an unknown supplier (SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE).

A draft purchase order (OrderOpen) of an organization from a supplier, with one purchase part (F7): the supplier's currency from its profile, else the buying policy's, else the organization's; the receiving facility given, else the policy's. The supplier check of the buying policy runs first: a Stop refuses with its reason (SUPPLIER_BLOCKED, SUPPLIER_SUSPENDED, SUPPLIER_UNAPPROVED), a Warn is a warning message and supplierResult. Requires PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), a supplier that is not one or is another organization's (SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE), another organization's facility (FACILITY_INVALID) and a currency that is not one (CURRENCY_INVALID).

A draft purchase order's name and receiving facility. Requires PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an order outside the user's organizations (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), one that is not a purchase order (NOT_PURCHASE) or has several parts (PURCHASE_PARTS), one that is not a draft (ORDER_NOT_DRAFT) and another organization's facility (FACILITY_INVALID).

A draft purchase order's line. A new line names a product usable for buying (check#ProductUsable, usage Purchase; PRODUCT_NOT_USABLE with its reason) at the supplier's price from the resolver unless a price is given (PRICE_UNAVAILABLE when there is none the user may read); a pack is ordered as its pack product. A line given by orderItemSeqId changes its quantity, unit, price, description, required date or cost centre. The cost centre is the organization or one that rolls up to it (COST_CENTER_INVALID). Requires PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an order outside the user's organizations (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), one that is not a draft (ORDER_NOT_DRAFT), a line not on it (ITEM_UNAVAILABLE), no product (PRODUCT_REQUIRED) and a quantity or price that is not a number (QUANTITY_INVALID).
A draft purchase order's line removed. Requires PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT; refuses as store#PurchaseOrderItem does.

Place a draft purchase order with lines (place#Order). The supplier check runs again: a Stop refuses, a Warn is a warning. Mantle's OrderPlaced rules then run; where the buying policy's approval gate is on, check#PurchaseApprovalRequired keeps autoApprove#Order from approving it (a prepaid or zero-total order too). Requires PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an order outside the user's organizations (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), one that is not a draft (ORDER_NOT_DRAFT) and one with no line (ORDER_EMPTY).

Cancel a purchase order nothing was received or billed on (cancel#Order), keeping the reason as an internal note. A partly received order closes its remainder (OrderServices.close#PurchaseRemainders) instead. Requires PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an order outside the user's organizations (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), no reason (REASON_REQUIRED), a completed, rejected or cancelled order (ORDER_NOT_OPEN), a received one (ORDER_RECEIVED) and a billed one (ORDER_BILLED).

A new draft purchase order with a purchase order's lines and parties (clone#Order, without payments, files or notes), for the same supplier, which the supplier check must not stop. A line whose product is no longer usable for buying is named in a warning and unusableItemSeqIds, to fix before placing. Requires PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an order outside the user's organizations (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE).

A purchase approver's decision on the step waiting of a placed purchase order at its revision (design ApprovalPolicies; impl-purchasing P3, P4). The steps are those the organization's approval policy selects for the order's amount, currency, categories and facility (PurchaseApprovalPolicy), else the no-policy rule's one step by any holder of PURCHASE_APPROVE. The decision is kept as a PurchaseApprovalDecision bound to the revision, the buying policy row and the approval policy's step. A refusal, with its reason, rejects the order (reject#Order, OrderPlaced to OrderRejected). An approval that leaves a step waiting sends it to its approvers (PurchaseOrderApproval) and answers pendingStepText; one that completes the last step reserves the budget of the lines with no request at the PO stage (mantle.other.BudgetServices.reserve#Commitment, keyed by the revision: a Stop refuses with BUDGET_EXCEEDED unless a BUDGET_OVERRIDE holder gives budgetOverrideReason, a Warn warns), then approve#Order approves the order (PURCHASE_ORDER_APPROVE for a purchase part; with the approval gate on it finds the approval complete). The same operation key answers the first result. Requires PURCHASE_APPROVE (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an order outside the user's organizations (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), one that is not placed (ORDER_NOT_PLACED), a revision that is not the current one, naming it (STALE_REVISION), an amount no policy row covers where the organization has some (POLICY_MISSING), a user the step does not name (NOT_ELIGIBLE), self-approval (SELF_APPROVAL), a second approval of one step (ALREADY_DECIDED), the approver of an earlier step where the step separates them (SEPARATION_REQUIRED), a refusal without a reason (REASON_REQUIRED) and a decision other than approve or refuse (DECISION_INVALID).

parameter.name: orderRevision
parameter.description: The revision reviewed; the current one when empty

parameter.name: budgetOverrideReason
parameter.description: Passes a budget Stop for a BUDGET_OVERRIDE holder

parameter.name: pendingStepText
parameter.description: The step still waiting, when the approval did not complete it

service.description: The approval gate's warning (design §6, D8): for each purchase part of the order whose buying organization's policy has approvalGateEnabled, PURCHASE_APPROVAL_REQUIRED unless the order's approval is complete at its current revision (every step of its approval policy, or the no-policy rule's one decision; P4). The Purchase SECA adds it to check#OrderPreApprove's approveWarnings, so autoApprove#Order does not approve the order, and approve#Order refuses on it. With the gate off (the default) nothing is added. It checks no permission: it runs as any user.

An approval step of an organization's purchase orders, requests, awards or suppliers, effective-dated (PurchaseApprovalPolicy): its amount band (from, included, up to thru, not included) and currency, an optional product category or facility, the step's sequence in its band, its approver (a user, else a user group's members, else any purchase approver of the organization, each holding PURCHASE_APPROVE), quorum, self-approval (Y, N, or empty for the buying policy's), separation from an earlier step's approver and expiry days. A new row starts at fromDate (now by default); given purchaseApprovalPolicyId, the next version of that row (it ends where the next starts), or with endPolicy Y that row ended at thruDate (now by default). Each key field is audit-logged with the reason. Requires PURCHASE_POLICY_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), no reason (REASON_REQUIRED), an unknown or ended row (POLICY_UNAVAILABLE, POLICY_ENDED), an invalid value or a start in the past (POLICY_INVALID), a band that overlaps another band of the same scope without being it, or a second row for one step of a band (POLICY_AMBIGUOUS), and a step with fewer eligible approvers than its quorum (NO_ELIGIBLE_APPROVER).

The approval of a source explained, writing nothing (design ApprovalPreview): a purchase order (orderId), a supplier of an organization (supplierPartyId), or an amount of an organization and source type (with currency, facility and category). Its revision, amount, the steps the approval policy selects (or the no-policy rule's one), each with its approver, quorum, who approved it at the revision, who may approve it, separation, self-approval, expiry and state (Done, Waiting, Next); a missing policy (rows in effect, none covering the amount); whether the user may decide the step waiting, or why not; and for a purchase order the budget's decision of its lines at the PO stage (check#Budget by account: OK, WARN, STOP, NONE), withheld (WITHHELD) from a user who is not a purchase approver or finance reader. Requires PURCHASE_APPROVE, PURCHASE_POLICY_EDIT or PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization, order or supplier outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE, SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE).

Submit a supplier of an organization for approval (R-PUR-15): its profile is put Pending (a profile row, store#SupplierProfile) and the step waiting goes to its approvers (PurchaseSupplierApproval). A supplier with no status, Pending, Rejected, or Suspended once its purchase block has ended may be submitted. Requires SUPPLIER_PROFILE_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), another organization's supplier (SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE), an approved one (ALREADY_APPROVED) and a suspended one whose block is in effect (SUPPLIER_BLOCKED).

A purchase approver's decision on a Pending supplier of an organization at its revision (the count of its profile rows), by the steps of the organization's supplier approval policy (PasSupplier), else one step by any purchase approver, checked as decide#PurchaseApproval checks an order's (approver, group, self-approval: the user who submitted it, separation, quorum). The decision is kept as a PurchaseApprovalDecision; the last step's approval sets the profile Approved and a refusal, with its reason, Rejected; a step left waiting goes to its approvers. Requires PURCHASE_APPROVE (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), another organization's supplier (SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE), one that is not Pending (NOT_PENDING), a revision that is not the current one, naming it (STALE_REVISION), POLICY_MISSING, NOT_ELIGIBLE, SELF_APPROVAL, ALREADY_DECIDED, SEPARATION_REQUIRED, REASON_REQUIRED and DECISION_INVALID.

Suspend a supplier of an organization: its profile Suspended with a dated purchase block (from now or fromDate, through thruDate when given) and its reason, so check#SupplierUsable stops it; its approval notices are read. Once the block ends it is submitted and approved again. Requires SUPPLIER_PROFILE_EDIT (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses an organization outside the user's (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), another organization's supplier (SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE) and no reason (REASON_REQUIRED).

The approve service of the PurchaseOrderApproval and PurchaseSupplierApproval topics (F23), which the framework's approve#NotificationMessage calls as the user: decide#PurchaseApproval (a purchase order) or decide#SupplierApproval (a supplier) at the revision in the message (sourceRevision), so a superseded revision is refused naming the current one. Requires PURCHASE_APPROVE (PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses another record (SOURCE_INVALID) and as the decide services do.

The refuse service of the PurchaseOrderApproval and PurchaseSupplierApproval topics (F23), with the reason: a refused purchase order is Rejected, a refused supplier Rejected (decide#PurchaseApproval, decide#SupplierApproval at the message's revision). Requires PURCHASE_APPROVE; refuses as approve#PurchaseSource does.

Internal to the Purchase SECA on increment#OrderRevision: a commercial change (not a status, file or note) of a purchase order supersedes the approval decisions of earlier revisions (supersededDate), and a placed order sent for approval starts again at its first step, sent to its approvers at the new revision. An order with neither a decision nor an approval notice returns at once. No permission of its own: it runs as any user. A failure to notify is logged and the change stays.
